text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said it upgraded the long and short term counterparty credit ratings of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp.
S&P said it upgraded the long term ratings for each bank to AA minus from A plus, and the short term ratings to A1 plus from A1.

The ratings agency also said it upgraded the ratings assigned to ANZ units Esanda Finance Corp Ltd and ANZ Banking Group (New Zealand) as well as Westpac units AGC, Challenge Bank Ltd, and Trust Bank New Zealand Ltd.
It said the ratings outlooks for ANZ, Westpac and related entities have been revised to stable from positive.
S&P said ANZ's profitability has rebounded over four consecutive half-year periods, while Westpac's profitability is satisfactory.
"The recent acquisitions of TBNZ (Trust Bank NZ) and Challenge are seen as favourable in reinforcing Westpac's domestic market position," it said.

"Amid intensified competition in the Australian and New Zealand banking industries, ANZ, Westpac and the other two major banks have demonstrated their ability to adapt and compete against both traditional and non-traditional rivals," S&P said.
The other major Australian banks are National Australia Bank Ltd and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
S&P said the banking sector has faced fierce competition in Australasia for mortgage loans, corporate lending, and retail savings.
"Nevertheless, recent indications are that the major banks are managing to maintain their market share of Australasian banking assets, which had been declining for several years."
S&P said the "superior diversity" of the majors in terms of geography, product mix, and finances supported its higher rating than that given to regional, or state-based, banks.

"Looking forward, Standard and Poor's is concerned about possible rising consumer and retail customer default, because of over-indebtedness, a situation which would be exacerbated by any economic slowdown in the near-to-medium term," it said.
